title: air liquide rises elliott reportedly builds stake pushes higher margins 2026 09 01
text:
Sept 1 (Reuters) - Shares in Air Liquide (AIRP.PA)
, opens new tab
 rose as much as 4.2% ‌on Tuesday after sources familiar with the matter said activist investor Elliott Investment Management had built a stake in the French industrial gases company.
Reuters reported on Monday that Elliott had been engaging with the €108 ​billion ($125 billion) company for months, pushing for changes aimed at making it more ​competitive.
Elliott's stake in Air Liquide could not immediately be determined. The hedge ⁠fund has urged management to improve margins, the sources said.
The Financial Times was the ​first to report that Elliott had built a stake in the French firm. Elliott declined ​to comment when contacted by Reuters, while Air Liquide did not respond to a request for comment.
Paris-based Air Liquide, which supplies gases including oxygen, nitrogen and hydrogen to factories and hospitals, has trailed ​rival Linde's profitability for years, although analysts see room for improvement.
Linde's operating margin stood ​at about 30% at mid-2026, compared with roughly 21% for Air Liquide, LSEG data showed.
In a note ‌to ⁠investors, J.P. Morgan analysts said one of the main drivers of the margin gap against Linde was Air Liquide's lower sales per employee, suggesting scope for further efficiency measures.
Elliott, among the world's biggest activist investors, has in recent years pushed for changes at companies ​including London Stock Exchange Group ​and electronic design ⁠automation software maker Synopsys.
The fund also targeted French spirits group Pernod Ricard in 2018, urging the maker of Martell cognac and Absolut vodka to ​boost profit margins.
Analysts at Bernstein said Air Liquide was not an ​obvious candidate ⁠for a traditional activist campaign.
However, they said Elliott's involvement could increase pressure on management and that a share buyback announcement at the company's scheduled capital markets day in October could ⁠act as ​a near-term catalyst for the stock.
Air Liquide shares, which ​have gained 20% this year, were up around 3% by 1102 GMT and on track for their biggest ​one-day gain in six months.
($1 = 0.8626 euros)
